dedupe_keys.name: planning of drinking fountains and misting systems in vienna institutions and environmental justice

description: This case study examines how the City of Vienna plans small-scale urban blue infrastructure in streets and parks, such as drinking fountains and misting systems, and how far principles of environmental justice are considered. It is a 2025 master's thesis in spatial research and planning at the University of Vienna by Maeve Sophie Hofer, supervised by Anna Kajosaari, with a German and English abstract. Such water features supply drinking water, cool the city, improve the quality of public space and support health and wellbeing, and are a relatively simple nature-based adaptation to climate change; yet blue and green infrastructure planning can reinforce existing inequalities. Using planning documents and expert interviews within the Austrian planning system, the thesis finds that formal and informal institutions strongly influence the planning of water features and the attention given to distributive, procedural and recognition justice. Coverage: the City of Vienna. Access: thesis record in u:theses with DOI 10.25365/thesis.79874. Licence: university thesis terms; free. Caveats: qualitative, one city. Simulation uses: policy evidence for siting cooling features in heat adaptation plans. Related records: the Naples climate shelters case study and the 3-30-300 datasets.
name: Planning of drinking fountains and misting systems in Vienna: institutions and environmental justice
organisations: University of Vienna (Maeve Sophie Hofer; supervisor Anna Kajosaari)
outcomes: Formal and informal institutions strongly shape how Vienna plans water features and how far distributive, procedural and recognition justice are considered, so local institutional structures must be addressed to plan equitable blue infrastructure.
